detail: Give the recent changes time to play out before adjusting them. He also said local officials "know their communities" (debate, paraphrase).

Long-term elimination of property taxes on primary residences: "You shouldn't have to rent your home from the government" (debate). Higher rates on institutional investors (site). Data centers would "pay 5x the normal property tax rate," with the money going "to give property tax relief to Iowa residents" (X, February 19, 2026). He has stated no plan for replacing local revenue.

"Those income cuts, I think, were reasonable. My criticism was not of the cuts, it was the fact that they have left us with a $1.3 billion budget deficit" (CBS2). His campaign told PolitiFact (September 17, 2026) he would not repeal the cuts. PolitiFact rated false Lahn's ad claim that Sand "wants to raise your taxes by $7,500 per year." "I would like to find a way to get the income taxes to zero," paid for by cutting waste, and "No sales tax, no income tax, no property tax raises" (ITR Foundation summary). He gives no timeline.

January 27, 2026: Radio Iowa reported he "would pull all COVID shots off the market in Iowa and end all childhood vaccine requirements connected to enrollment in Iowa schools." September 2026, KCCI interview: answered "Yes" when asked if he would support eliminating school vaccine requirements. This comes from a transcript published by the Iowa Democratic Party (partisan); Studio 31 corroborates it. Later, on CBS2: "My very firm belief is that there are benefits from vaccination, of course" and "Do I think that there's potential benefits from future mRNA technology? Of course there could be."

A 5% increase in state aid in year one (debate). ESA rules: "Requiring annual audits," "Limiting tuition increases," "Implementing income limits," and ending the Odyssey arrangement (Accountability plan). "The wealthiest folks in Iowa, God bless them, good for them, they don't need help to send their kids to private school" (debate). "If you take public money, you take the public." He is not proposing repeal: "I support Iowa families making the decision that's best for their kids." Documented action: his auditor's ESA report.
